caption:
Oracle cut over 1,000 roles in India last month. The layoff trackers are still updating. Indian IT headcount commentary is landing this quarter, and the question in every leadership room is the same: which managers do we still need.

Understand how that decision actually gets made. Nobody opens your output file. They go off an impression — formed in meetings, built over months, of whether you are the person who holds the room or the person who fills a seat in it.

For years, being competent but invisible cost you a promotion. In a thinning org, it costs you the job.

This is a bearing problem, not a performance problem. How you enter. How you hold the pause before you answer. Whether your voice drops at the end of a sentence or climbs. In command, a leader who cannot be read cannot be followed. Boardrooms are no different.

The work is learnable. Most people never learn it because nobody ever told them it was the work.

topic.title: AI squeeze on Indian middle management
topic.angle: Lumina's buyer is the competent-but-invisible manager, and in a thinning org invisibility stops costing a promotion and starts costing the job, because the person deciding who stays works off an impression of indispensability formed in meetings rather than an output file.
topic.why_now: Oracle cut 1,000+ Indian tech roles roughly four weeks ago, layoff trackers were updating as recently as yesterday, and Indian IT quarterly results and headcount commentary are landing now, putting the 'where did the managers go' conversation at peak volume.

rationale: A stark text-only visual matches the no-nonsense command tone and lets the single hard line about invisibility carry the post without decoration.
